Lemma
[Simplicity makes the linearisation injective]

↗ def:simple-eigenpair ↗ def:eigen-linearisation

If $(S,v,\lambda )$ is simple and $\langle v_0,v\rangle =1$, then $L_{S,v,\lambda ,v_0}$ is injective and therefore bijective.

Proof

↗ def:simple-eigenpair ↗ def:eigen-linearisation \sketch If $L(w,\mu )=0$, pair $Sw-\lambda w=\mu v$ with $v$. Symmetry and $Sv=\lambda v$ give $\mu \langle v,v\rangle =0$, hence $\mu =0$. Simplicity gives $w=cv$, and $0=\langle v_0,w\rangle =c$. Thus the kernel is trivial; equal finite dimensions give surjectivity.

□
